sections.h2: Where is Craig County, Oklahoma, and what does it include?
sections.html:
Craig County sits in the northeast corner of Oklahoma, with Kansas along its northern edge. It covers 762.71 square miles, and Vinita is the county seat, according to the Oklahoma Historical Society encyclopedia.

Five incorporated towns sit inside the county lines: Bluejacket, Big Cabin, Ketchum, Vinita and Welch. Smaller places such as White Oak, Wimer and Hudson are unincorporated or have faded. A house in any of these places is billed by the same county treasurer, even though the city or school levy on the bill differs.

The land is mostly rolling prairie, with sandstone hills and long mounds in the west and a rougher stretch called the Neosho Lowlands in the east and south. Big Cabin Creek drains the southern part. For a seller, that mix means a Craig County parcel can be a town lot, a few acres of pasture or a hay field, and the tax paperwork for each can look quite different.

sections.h2: How did Craig County come to be?
sections.html:
The state constitutional convention created Craig County, naming it for Granville Craig, a Cherokee farmer who lived near Welch and Bluejacket from 1873. Before that, the area belonged to the Delaware and Cooweescoowee districts of the Cherokee Nation.

Two railroads shaped the map. The Missouri, Kansas and Texas line ran north to south in 1871, and the Atlantic and Pacific line came east to west the same year. Vinita grew where they crossed. The Vinita entry notes that the town was incorporated under a Cherokee Council law, and that it became the governmental center when the county was formed in 1907.

  • 1871: two rail lines reach the area.
  • 1907: statehood, with Vinita as the seat.
  • 1935: the Grand River Dam Authority begins the Pensacola Dam, which forms Grand Lake O' the Cherokees.
  • 2020: the census counted 14,104 residents in the county.

The county population peaked near 21,000 around 1940 and has stayed between roughly 14,000 and 15,000 since 1980.

sections.h2: What drives the Craig County economy?
sections.html:
Farming, ranching, energy and public employers have carried Craig County for a century. The state encyclopedia lists hay, soybeans, wheat, sorghum and corn as the main crops, and says many ranches remain active in the western half of the county.

Coal was mined by underground and surface methods after the Civil War, and an oil refinery operated west of Vinita as early as 1911. The 1940 completion of Pensacola Dam brought the Grand River Dam Authority, Northeast Oklahoma Electric Cooperative and KAMO Electric into the local economy, and the Vinita encyclopedia says the co-ops still keep significant operations in town.

Government work has also mattered. Eastern State Hospital opened in 1912 on the northeast edge of Vinita and was one of the county's largest employers until operations shrank in the late 1990s. A state corrections facility later took over part of that land.

sections.h2: How do roads and rail affect homes in Craig County?
sections.html:
Craig County sits on one of the busiest corridors in the northeast part of the state. Interstate 44, the Will Rogers Turnpike, crosses the county on its way to Tulsa, and U.S. Highways 59, 60 and 69 run through it along with Historic U.S. 66.

RouteWhere it goes in Craig County
Interstate 44Northeast to southwest across the county toward Tulsa
U.S. 60West through White Oak to Nowata
U.S. 69South through Big Cabin into Mayes County
Historic U.S. 66Through Vinita, where four listed Route 66 sites stand

Vinita is about sixty miles from Tulsa and sixty from Joplin, Missouri, and the BNSF and Union Pacific lines still cross there.

sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Craig County?
sections.html:
The Craig County Treasurer collects the tax, and the County Assessor sets the value it is based on. The treasurer's own site describes the job as collecting taxes certified by the assessor on real estate, personal property and public utilities.

After collection, the money goes out to the county, towns and school districts under budgets approved by the Excise Board. Your bill therefore blends several levies, and the treasurer does not choose the rate.

OfficeDetails
Craig County Treasurer210 W. Delaware, Suite 104, Vinita, OK 74301; 918-256-2286
HoursMonday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM
Drop boxNear the west doors of the courthouse
Online lookupTax roll inquiry on oktaxrolls.com

The treasurer lists courthouse closures through the year, including a closure on August 5, 2026 for the rodeo parade. If you plan to pay in person near a holiday, call first. We could not find an official Craig County assessor website, so confirm the assessor's phone number and hours with the courthouse before you visit.

sections.h2: When are Craig County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Oklahoma law, 68 O.S. 2913, sets two payment points: half before January 1, and the rest before April 1. If less than half has been paid by December 31, the whole year's levy turns delinquent on January 1.

The Craig County treasurer's page did not list a separate calendar, so the statewide statute is the rule to follow. Neighboring county offices add a monthly penalty to late balances, but we did not confirm Craig County's exact penalty or payment fees, so ask the office for a current payoff figure rather than counting on an estimate.

  • The state rule says a missing statement does not extend the due date.
  • Back taxes can be marked on a statement, which means the printed amount may not be the full balance.
  • A seller who is behind should ask for a written total good through the expected closing date.

sections.h2: How do you protest a valuation in Craig County?
sections.html:
You protest first with the county assessor, in writing, within 30 calendar days of the date the valuation notice was mailed. The Oklahoma Tax Commission's Form 974 spells out the process under 68 O.S. 2876.

  1. File Form 974 with the assessor and state what you believe the market value is.
  2. Back it up with a recent sale, comparable sales or an appraisal.
  3. Attend the informal hearing, which can be held by phone if you ask.
  4. Wait for the assessor's written decision, due within seven calendar days of the hearing.
  5. If you disagree, appeal to the county board of equalization on Form 976 within 15 calendar days of the decision mailing.

If the assessor did not change your value from the year before, the form allows a protest up to the first Monday in April. The form also says proceedings must wrap up by May 31 or the board's adjournment date. Miss the 30-day window and the proposed value becomes final for that tax year.

A Craig County assessor post on social media says notices of change in valuation went out in early February in recent years and that bills arrive in November. That is not an official page, so treat the timing as a clue and check the date printed on your own notice.

sections.h2: Can unpaid city charges follow a Craig County house?
sections.html:
Yes. City and town charges such as weed cutting, cleanup, paving and nuisance abatement are sent to the county treasurer once they are delinquent, and they become a lien on the property account.

That detail matters for sellers of neglected or vacant houses in Vinita, Welch, Ketchum, Bluejacket and Big Cabin. A title company will see an unpaid mowing bill on the tax account. Ask the treasurer for a full account printout before you list or accept an offer.

The treasurer also manages county-owned property acquired at annual sales for delinquent taxes and may sell it with approval from the Board of County Commissioners. If a house you own is far behind, that sale process is the end of the road, so it is worth acting early.

sections.h2: How does tax get handled when a Craig County house sells?
sections.html:
At closing, the title or escrow company asks the treasurer what is owed and pays it from the seller's proceeds if the amount is outstanding.

A cash sale can move fast, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. Still, a few steps do not go away:

  • Get a payoff or tax certificate from the treasurer.
  • Clear any special assessment liens.
  • Sign a deed that meets the clerk's formatting rules.
  • Pay documentary stamp tax when the deed is recorded.

Craig County's deed records are kept by the County Clerk at 210 West Delaware Avenue, Suite 103, Vinita, phone 918-256-2507, open 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. The online index on okcountyrecords.com goes back to October 1956. Under 68 O.S. 3201, documentary stamp tax is 75 cents for each $500 of consideration, and it applies when the price is above $100.

sections.h2: What do Craig County sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Most Craig County sellers deal with age, distance and paperwork. Many homes are older, many parcels are rural, and many owners live elsewhere after inheriting a place from family.

  • Inherited houses where heirs are spread across several states.
  • Rural lots where the legal description includes acreage and mineral questions.
  • Lake-area properties tied to Grand Lake, which the Pensacola Dam created.
  • Houses with unpaid city charges or back taxes.

Whichever route you pick, start with the treasurer's balance and the clerk's records so nothing surprises you in the last week.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property tax in Craig County, Oklahoma?
faqs.a: Call the Craig County Treasurer at 918-256-2286 for bills and payments. The office is at 210 W. Delaware, Suite 104 in Vinita and is open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Valuation questions go to the county assessor at the courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Craig County valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file a written protest with the assessor. If your value did not change from last year, the form allows a protest until the first Monday in April.

faqs.q: Does Craig County list a late fee on its treasurer site?
faqs.a: The pages we reviewed did not state a penalty rate, so call the treasurer for an exact payoff. State law makes the whole levy delinquent on January 1 unless half has been paid before then, and the remainder is due before April 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Craig County house with taxes still owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is normally paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Ask the treasurer for a written total and clear any city special assessments that were certified to the county.
